newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US income, spending seen easing in March.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US income, spending seen easing in March.

text.p: U.S. personal income and spending probably eased somewhat in March after a particularly strong February, setting the trend for a slowdown in future months, economists said on Tuesday.
Last month, personal income and consumption, set for release Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, grew 0.4 percent and 0.5 percent respectively, according to a Reuters poll of economic forecasters.
That compares with 0.9-percent earnings growth in February and a 0.3-percent spending figure likely to be revised higher in light of February's stellar retail sales performance.

"Really what's happening is that January and February were just so strong in every way that some of the slowdown (in March) is inevitable," said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.
But Kretzmer said he would not expect a particularly weak report, especially because of strength in auto sales and service-sector consumption.
While spending growth should remain solid, the income data may be more difficult to process. Unusually high financial services bonuses should skew the report, analysts said.
"The bonus payments are stronger than in past years because corporate profits are stronger," said Michael Strauss, chief economists at Sanwa Securities (USA) Co.
"The seasonals are correct in anticipating some of the bonus payments, but they should be greater than in past years," he added.

Looking ahead, economists projected further moderation in April. Hours worked declined in March, suggesting slower earnings growth, while retail sales appear slower in April, pointing to weaker consumption, some said.
The backward-looking personal income and spending report provides little new insight into the future of Federal Reserve monetary policy, economists said.

Key indicators to watch ahead of the May 20 Fed policy meeting include some portions of Thursday's National Association of Purchasing Management monthly survey, Friday's report on April employment conditions and the May 13 retail sales release, economists said.
